overall: Tomorrow (Saturday, June 27) is expected to be a hot, mostly sunny day in Atlanta with a slight chance of afternoon showers or thunderstorms between 2–3pm, carrying only a 20% precipitation probability. forecast_obs_notes: Source models show moderate spread with a warm-side bias in most guidance: HRRR and NBM are tightly clustered at ~91.3°F and ~90.4°F respectively, ECMWF agrees at ~90.0°F, while GFS is the clear cold outlier at ~85.9°F and WEATHER_COM sits in the middle at ~88.1°F. The GFS divergence is the key source of uncertainty, but the majority of models favor the 89–92°F range, lending moderate overall confidence.
max_temp_prediction: The active Kalshi market uses odd buckets, and the model ensemble strongly favors the 87–88°F odd bucket at 59.3% (Tier 1 — high confidence, large gap of 10.2pp over the next bucket). Despite the NWS narrative calling for a high near 92°F and most NWP models clustering around 90–91°F, the full ensemble expected TMAX of 84.3°F (obs-adjusted) pulls the probability mass lower, and the odd-bucket distribution reflects this tension by concentrating weight in the 87–88°F range. Best point estimate is approximately 89°F, balancing model-consensus warmth (~90°F from ECMWF/NBM/HRRR) against the ensemble's obs-corrected lower expectation and the high-probability odd bucket signal.
